question_record.context: There has been a sequence of alerts indicating potential human-operated malicious activity which might lead to ransomware or other payloads being installed on target devices. Some of the notable processes executed include `powershell.exe` to disable real-time monitoring, `psexesvc.exe`, and `rubeus.exe` used to extract service tickets. These actions were observed on host `vnevado-win10b` and involved accounts such as `kyleg` (AadUserId: 97e6a954-b6bd-48a5-808c-bd8464cce677) and `fk8mq` (Sid: S-1-5-21-1540151660-3530000288-105586595-1517). One particular instance included the extraction of credentials using the Rubeus tool, which was later executed via command line by the user `lucasb`.
question_record.question: Which suspicious service was started using the `net.exe` command?
solution: A suspicious service was launched with command line `net.exe start ntds` at `2024-06-27t14:34:44.6620407z`, with Process ID `3400`.
Multiple dual-purpose tools, such as `powershell.exe`, were dropped on the device.
Potential human-operated malicious activity was detected involving the execution of `rubeus.exe`.

105.name: Potential human-operated malicious activity
105.description: A sequence of alerts that might be indicative of human operated malicious activity was observed on this device. This activity might lead to ransomware or other payloads installed on target devices.

62.name: Multiple dual-purpose tools were dropped
62.description:
Multiple known public tools, which could also be used for malicious reasons were dropped on this device.
Attackers might download or copy multiple dual-purpose tools to the target device to perform various attack stages including, credential theft, privilege escalation, and lateral movement.

12.name: Suspicious service launched
12.description: A suspicious service was started on this device. Attackers might use services to launch malicious commands or programs. This technique is used to maintain persistence or elevate privileges on the target device.
